title: Plan the statusline by default, add --no-statusline, and keep the manifest converging
action:
SLICE 1, part 2 of 4. Depends on sbd-2's hooks_wiring API (STATUSLINE_COMMAND, statusline_settings_absent, merge_statusline_settings) — it is already merged, use it. Touch NO other file; apply.rs and onboard/tests.rs are other cells.

A. mod.rs — the opt-out.
  - `parse_args` gains `--no-statusline`, arm placed beside `--no-claude-md` (l.170-171). Keep parse_args_rejects_unknown_flags_and_bad_runtimes green.
  - `Options` gains `statusline: bool`, computed as: NOT --no-statusline AND NOT the project's recorded opt-out. The recorded opt-out is `.bee/config.json` `"statusline": false`, read exactly the way merge.rs::host_shell_is_powershell reads `host_shell` (merge.rs:48-58) — a project-level preference bee READS and never writes. Absent or unrecognised -> true.
  - ALSO false when `merge::host_shell_is_powershell(&repo_root)` is true. There is no PowerShell variant of this bash script; a failed hook is silent but a failed statusLine is drawn on every prompt, and a bare `bash` on native Windows can resolve to the WSL launcher which cannot open a C:\… path (this repo already warns about that at hooks_wiring.rs:350). Emit a notice so the skip is visible rather than mysterious — follow how onboard/notices.rs already words its notices.
  - Update the module header comment (l.5-8) which enumerates what onboarding manages.

B. plan.rs — the plan.
  - Compute ONE value per run, before stage 3b: `let statusline = opts.statusline && (hw::statusline_opt_in(repo_root) || hw::statusline_settings_absent(repo_root));`  This single value gates stage 3b, the new item, AND build_managed_versions. Do not recompute it from statusline_opt_in alone anywhere — the pre-apply opt-in is false on a fresh host, and feeding that to the manifest makes the post-apply recheck report changes_needed for ever, which scripts/install.sh turns into a FAILED INSTALL.
  - Stage 3b (l.785): gate on that value instead of `hw::statusline_opt_in(repo_root)`.
  - New plan item `merge_statusline_settings` targeting ".claude/settings.json", pushed when the value is true AND hw::statusline_settings_absent(repo_root). Push it AFTER stage 5's merge_repo_hook_settings item so the two writers of that one file run in a known order.
  - `build_managed_versions` / `subset_managed` (l.256, l.316, l.966-990): feed them the same single value in place of today's `hw::statusline_opt_in(repo_root)` at l.966.
  - Gate NONE of this on opts.repo_hooks or opts.plugin_source. A Claude plugin cannot supply a statusLine, so a plugin-first host gets the display only if onboarding writes it, and 'plugin-first never touches settings.json' is not a property anything relies on (bee dev plugin-distribution --apply already rewrites that file via clean_hook_config).

C. The help surfaces, so the flag is not a secret.
  - router.rs:98-99 usage string: append [--no-statusline].
  - src/generated/registry_payload.json, command "onboard": add a "no-statusline" boolean property after "no-claude-md", description: "Skip the default status display: neither the .claude/settings.json statusLine entry nor statusline-command.sh is written."

No new tests in this cell — sbd-5 owns onboard/tests.rs. Keep the crate compiling and every existing test green.

truths: One `statusline` value per run feeds stage 3b, the new plan item, and build_managed_versions.
--no-statusline and .bee/config.json statusline:false both suppress every statusline action.
A PowerShell host is skipped with a visible notice.
The new plan item is not gated on repo_hooks or plugin_source.
router.rs usage and the registry payload both list the flag.

sbd-3 and sbd-4 were planned as separate cells but cannot be green apart: the plan item and its apply case are one behavior. sbd-3 was committed red-in-isolation and proven only once sbd-4 landed — the plan was wrong about a fact

mistakes.better: one cell for the plan-and-apply pair would have been honest
